items.new_note: Luke 24:43 — *And he took it, and did eat before them.* Ignatius writes that "after His resurrection He [both] ate with them and drank with them as one in the flesh" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:3), the same meal Luke sets down, and it answers those who say He suffered "in semblance" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:2).
items.new_member_note: Luke 24:43 — *And he took it, and did eat before them.* Ignatius writes that "after His resurrection He [both] ate with them and drank with them as one in the flesh" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:3), the same meal Luke sets down.

items.new_note: Isaiah 53:5 — *But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.* Ignatius speaks of "His most blessed passion" and says Yahusha (Jesus) was "truly nailed up in the flesh for our sakes" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:1); the prophet had written long before of one wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our iniquities.
items.new_member_note: Isaiah 53:5 — *But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.* Ignatius speaks of "His most blessed passion" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:1), foretold by the prophet.

items.new_note: Malachi 3:3 — *And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto Yahuah (LORD) an offering in righteousness.* Polycarp in the fire was, in the witness's words, "not like flesh burning, but like [a loaf in the oven or like] gold and silver refined in a furnace" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:15), which is the picture Malachi gives of the Refiner who purges the sons of Levi as gold and silver, that they may offer an offering in righteousness.
items.new_member_note: Malachi 3:3 — *And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto Yahuah (LORD) an offering in righteousness.* Polycarp in the fire was "not like flesh burning, but like [a loaf in the oven or like] gold and silver refined in a furnace" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:15), the offering in righteousness the Refiner purges out.

items.new_note: Romans 8:17 — *And if children, then heirs; heirs of Elohim (God), and joint-heirs with Messiah (Christ); if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.* Polycarp is bound to the stake "like a noble ram out of a great flock for an offering, a burnt sacrifice made ready and acceptable to Elohim (God)" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:14), and that is the suffering with Messiah that Paul says ends in being glorified together.
items.new_member_note: Romans 8:17 — *And if children, then heirs; heirs of Elohim (God), and joint-heirs with Messiah (Christ); if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.* Polycarp, "a burnt sacrifice made ready and acceptable to Elohim (God)" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:14), is the suffering with Messiah that Paul says ends in being glorified together.

items.new_note: Revelation 2:10 — *Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.* The Messiah spoke this to the church in Smyrna, Polycarp's own city, and Polycarp's answer to the proconsul, "How then can I blaspheme my King who saved me?" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:9), is that faithfulness unto death.

items.flag: The quoted words 'How then can I blaspheme my King who saved me?' sit in Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:9, not 1:8 (the card's own verse); cited 1:9.

items.new_note: Deuteronomy 10:12 — *And now, Yashar'el (Israel), what doth Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) require of thee, but to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thy heart and with all thy soul,* Moses asks Yashar'el to fear, to walk in all His ways, to love and to serve; the Shepherd gives Hermas the same charge in fewer words: "Believe Him therefore, and fear Him, and in this fear be continent," and he shall live "if thou keep this commandment" (Hermas 6:1).
items.new_member_note: Deuteronomy 10:12 — *And now, Yashar'el (Israel), what doth Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) require of thee, but to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thy heart and with all thy soul,* Moses asks Yashar'el to fear, to walk in all His ways, to love and to serve; the Shepherd gives Hermas the same charge: "Believe Him therefore, and fear Him" (Hermas 6:1).

items.new_note: Matthew 19:17 — *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* The Shepherd tells Hermas, "Thou shalt live," if "thou keep my commandments and walk in them" (Hermas 9:2), and Yahusha (Jesus) gave the same road to life: if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.
items.new_member_note: Matthew 19:17 — *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* The Shepherd's "if thou keep my commandments and walk in them" (Hermas 9:2) is the road to life Yahusha (Jesus) gave: keep the commandments.

items.new_note: Matthew 19:9 — *And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.* The Shepherd rules, "Let him divorce her," and "if after divorcing his wife he shall marry another, he likewise committeth adultery" (Hermas 9:1); that is the ruling Yahusha (Jesus) gives here: divorce for fornication, and marrying another is adultery.
items.new_member_note: Matthew 19:9 — *And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.* The Shepherd's "Let him divorce her," and "if after divorcing his wife he shall marry another, he likewise committeth adultery" (Hermas 9:1) is the ruling Yahusha (Jesus) gave.
items.flag: Old note said 'verbatim in substance' and 'exact ruling'; softened. Hermas 9:1 allows return after repentance (not quoted); Matthew 19:9 canon verse unchanged.

items.new_note: Deuteronomy 10:20 — *Thou shalt fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God); him shalt thou serve, and to him shalt thou cleave, and swear by his name.* The Shepherd says, "if thou fear Yahuah (Lord), thou shalt be master over the devil" (Hermas 12:1), and it rests on Moses' charge to fear Yahuah and cleave to Him alone.
items.new_member_note: Deuteronomy 10:20 — *Thou shalt fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God); him shalt thou serve, and to him shalt thou cleave, and swear by his name.* The Shepherd's "if thou fear Yahuah (Lord), thou shalt be master over the devil" (Hermas 12:1) rests on Moses' charge to fear and cleave to Yahuah alone.

items.new_note: Proverbs 8:13 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.* The Shepherd says, "But fear thou the works of the devil, for they are evil" (Hermas 12:1), and that is the fear of Yahuah that Proverbs defines as the hatred of evil.
items.new_member_note: Proverbs 8:13 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.* The Shepherd's "But fear thou the works of the devil, for they are evil" (Hermas 12:1) is the fear of Yahuah that Proverbs defines as the hatred of evil.

items.new_note: Isaiah 1:17 — *Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.* Among the works of the good the Shepherd tells Hermas to do are "to minister to widows, to visit the orphans and the needy" and "to practice righteousness" (Hermas 13:1); the prophet had already said to learn to do well, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless and plead for the widow.
items.new_member_note: Isaiah 1:17 — *Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.* The Shepherd's "to minister to widows, to visit the orphans and the needy" (Hermas 13:1) is the prophet's call to learn to do well.

items.new_note: Isaiah 1:16 — *Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;* The Shepherd's charge, "Be temperate as to what is evil, and do it not" (Hermas 13:1), is the prophet's call to cease to do evil, spoken to a people he would cleanse.
items.new_member_note: Isaiah 1:16 — *Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;* The Shepherd's "Be temperate as to what is evil, and do it not" (Hermas 13:1) is the prophet's call to cease to do evil, spoken to a people he would cleanse.

items.new_note: Hebrews 11:6 — *But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to Elohim (God) must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.* The Shepherd tells Hermas to "put on faith, for it is strong, and trust Elohim (God) that thou wilt receive all thy petitions which thou askest" (Hermas 14:1), and it rests on the same foundation: he that cometh to Elohim must believe He rewards the seeker.
items.new_member_note: Hebrews 11:6 — *But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to Elohim (God) must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.* The Shepherd's "put on faith, for it is strong, and trust Elohim (God) that thou wilt receive all thy petitions which thou askest" (Hermas 14:1) rests on the same foundation: he that cometh to Elohim must believe He rewards the seeker.

items.new_note: Mark 11:24 — *Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.* The Shepherd says the complete in the faith "receive, because they ask without wavering, nothing doubting" (Hermas 14:1), and it is Yahusha's (Jesus') command to believe when you pray, that you may have; it ain't new.
items.new_member_note: Mark 11:24 — *Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.* The Shepherd's "they receive, because they ask without wavering, nothing doubting" (Hermas 14:1) is Yahusha's (Jesus') command to believe when you pray, that you may have; it ain't new.

items.new_note: Matthew 21:22 — *And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.* The Shepherd's promise, "ask of Yahuah (Lord), and thou shalt receive all things, and shalt lack nothing of all thy petitions, if thou ask of Yahuah (Lord) nothing wavering" (Hermas 14:1), is Yahusha's (Jesus') own word: ask in prayer, believing, and receive.
items.new_member_note: Matthew 21:22 — *And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.* The Shepherd's "thou shalt receive all things" (Hermas 14:1) for the one who asks nothing wavering is Yahusha's (Jesus') own word: ask in prayer, believing, and receive.

items.new_note: James 3:15 — *This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.* The Shepherd says "this doubtful-mindedness is a daughter of the devil" and that it "is an earthly spirit from the devil, and hath no power" (Hermas 14:1); that matches Ya'aqov's (James's) verdict on what is earthly and devilish, not from above.
items.new_member_note: James 3:15 — *This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.* The Shepherd calls doubtful-mindedness "a daughter of the devil" and "an earthly spirit from the devil" (Hermas 14:1); Ya'aqov (James) gives the same verdict on what is earthly and devilish, not from above.

items.new_note: James 1:7 — *For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of Yahuah (Lord).* The Shepherd's ruling on the waverer, "thou shalt surely receive none of thy petitions" (Hermas 14:1), is Ya'aqov's (James's) own sentence on the man who doubts; it ain't new.
items.new_member_note: James 1:7 — *For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of Yahuah (Lord).* The Shepherd's "thou shalt surely receive none of thy petitions" (Hermas 14:1) for the one who wavers is Ya'aqov's (James's) own sentence on the man who doubts; it ain't new.

items.new_note: Deuteronomy 18:21 — *And if thou say in thine heart, How shall we know the word which Yahuah (LORD) hath not spoken?* Hermas asks, "shall a man know who of them is a prophet, and who a false prophet?" (Hermas 16:1), which is the very question Moses set before Yashar'el; it ain't new.
items.new_member_note: Deuteronomy 18:21 — *And if thou say in thine heart, How shall we know the word which Yahuah (LORD) hath not spoken?* Hermas asks, "shall a man know who of them is a prophet, and who a false prophet?" (Hermas 16:1), the very question Moses set before Yashar'el; it ain't new.

items.new_note: 1 Peter 5:9 — *Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.* The angel says, "If then ye resist him, he will be vanquished and will flee from you disgraced" (Hermas 17:5), and Kepha (Peter) gives the same charge: resist the devil, stedfast in the faith.
items.new_member_note: 1 Peter 5:9 — *Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.* The angel's "If then ye resist him, he will be vanquished" (Hermas 17:5) is Kepha's (Peter's) charge to resist, stedfast in the faith.

items.new_note: James 4:7 — *Submit yourselves therefore to Elohim (God). Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.* The angel of repentance says, "Fear him not therefore; and he will flee from you" (Hermas 17:4), which is Ya'aqov's (James's) word in other words: resist the devil and he will flee.
items.new_member_note: James 4:7 — *Submit yourselves therefore to Elohim (God). Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.* The angel of repentance's "Fear him not therefore; and he will flee from you" (Hermas 17:4) is Ya'aqov's (James's) word: resist the devil and he will flee.

items.new_note: 1 Peter 5:9 — *Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.* The Shepherd bids Hermas, "having armed thyself with the fear of Yahuah (Lord), resist them," and the evil desire "shall flee far from thee" (Hermas 17:2); that is Kepha's (Peter's) charge, resist stedfast in the faith.
items.new_member_note: 1 Peter 5:9 — *Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.* The Shepherd's "having armed thyself with the fear of Yahuah (Lord), resist them" (Hermas 17:2) is Kepha's (Peter's) charge to resist, stedfast in the faith.

items.new_note: 1 Timothy 6:8 — *And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.* The "a competency which is sufficient for thee" that Hermas commands the sojourner to prepare (Hermas 18:1) is Sha'ul's own contentment with food and raiment, not the heaping up of estates.
items.new_member_note: 1 Timothy 6:8 — *And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.* The "a competency which is sufficient for thee" that Hermas commands the sojourner to prepare (Hermas 18:1) is Sha'ul's own contentment with food and raiment.

items.new_note: Isaiah 58:6 — *Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?* The Shepherd's "do no wickedness in thy life, and serve Yahuah (Lord) with a pure heart; observe His commandments and walk in His ordinances" (Hermas 22:1) is the prophet's own fast that looses wickedness; the true fast was never mere abstinence.
